s63a2870f852ac8: Viewing overall trends, a significant change this year is that AI is gradually moving from the application layer to the core position of the cloud native system. In past years, KubeCon discussions focused more on containers, microservices, and platform engineering. This year, whether in keynotes, AI-related sessions, or Project Pavilion project distribution, a clearer signal is being conveyed:
sa61b27f08528cd: AI is becoming one of the main themes in the Kubernetes ecosystem
sa677cd99439c70: Meanwhile, the role of GPUs is also changing. It's no longer just an "acceleration device" on a single node, but is being redefined as a foundational resource that needs scheduling, sharing, and fine-grained management. GPU virtualization, resource utilization, multi-tenant isolation, and scheduling strategies are becoming key issues in AI infrastructure—and these are exactly what HAMi focuses on.
